analyst_observations: Direction detection bug showed the largest efficiency gain: with-skill used 67k tokens in 352s (15 tool uses) vs without-skill 89k tokens in 595s (24 tool uses) — 40% faster, 25% fewer tokens
Extending DnD showed the strongest tool-use reduction: 27 vs 52 tool calls — the skill provided a file map that eliminated exploratory searches

Pending tree flicker was the closest result: both identified the same root cause (await cancelQueries timing gap). Without-skill was slightly faster here (133s vs 165s) and used fewer tokens (40k vs 51k) — the skill's context didn't provide a shortcut for this specific investigation

Backend rejection was the only eval where pass rates differed: without-skill missed the frontend prevention layer (collision detection type filtering). The skill's architecture overview helped the with-skill agent recognize this defense-in-depth design

Non-discriminating assertions: 14 of 15 assertions passed for both configurations — the assertions may be too easy. Only 'mentions-frontend-prevention' in eval 3 discriminated. Consider harder assertions that test depth of understanding (e.g., 'explains WHY centerCrossing uses overlap gate margins' rather than just 'mentions collisionDetection.ts')
The with-skill runs show lower variance in duration (stddev 101s vs 217s) suggesting more predictable exploration paths
